standard.name: OpenSSF Secure Supply Chain Consumption Framework

requirements.verification: Dependencies enter through npm, PyPI, crates.io, and GitHub Actions under the source policy.
Exact locks and CI caches reduce upstream outages, but this single-repository project does not operate an enterprise binary repository manager.
requirements.gap: A public OSS project cannot require every consumer to use an organization-controlled artifact proxy.

requirements.verification: PR dependency review blocks high severity regressions; pip-audit and cargo audit run on schedules and pushes.
Every approved runtime/build supplier has an SPDX license and an explicit approval decision in the supplier register.
Dependabot maintenance signals and release-age review reduce end-of-life exposure; no universal multi-ecosystem EOL database is authoritative.
requirements.gap: EOL status requires reviewer judgment at dependency-update time.

requirements.verification: The release builder emits CycloneDX 1.6 and SPDX 3.0 SBOMs plus deterministic payload inventory.
The incident-response runbook covers supplier compromise, advisory triage, deny-list actions, consumer notification, and artifact revocation.
SECURITY documents severity thresholds and the requirement to ship fixed versions.
Dependabot tracks GitHub Actions, pip, npm, cargo, and container inputs weekly.
The S2C2F prerequisite requiring two-person PR review is unavailable in the current single-maintainer repository.
requirements.gap: Dependency review still runs on every PR, but the specified two-person display prerequisite is unmet.

requirements.verification: Approved source hosts are declared, lock files are required, npm lifecycle scripts are prohibited, and CI dependencies use pinned requirement files.
Release checksums, payload tree digests, lock files, and OIDC attestations bind consumed and produced artifacts to immutable identities.
Package sources are HTTPS-only, exact registries are configured, npm install scripts are blocked, and lock/version pinning is tested.
